To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the estrogen receptor (ER) gene, ER-alpha, is a critical gene in the control of female sexual behavior, 2) the TR-beta thyroid hormone receptor gene, is also a key gene in the control, of female reproductive behaviors, 3) the ER-alpha gene and the TR-beta gene act in a complementary manner to regulate lordosis, 4) the TR-beta gene acts in the forebrain to regulate lordosis behavior, 5) the TR-beta protein is

the genes ER-alpha, TR-beta and the estrogen-regulated protein, progestin receptor, are necessary and sufficient for estrogenic facilitation of female sexual behavior; that the genes ER-beta and TR-alpha are not required for this behavior, but may be required for the facilitation of sexual motivation; and that the genes TR-alpha and TR-beta are necessary and sufficient, respectively, for the expression of the TH-induced facilitation of lordosis behavior.
the genes encoding the classical estrogen receptor (ER) and the TH receptor (TR-beta) are necessary for female sexual behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie sexual behavior.
the genetic, hormonal, and neuronal mechanisms underlying sexual arousal and the motivational state that is the necessary intermediate between stimulus and response.
the genetic, neural and psychological underpinnings of sexual arousal, and the mechanisms by which hormones and genes influence behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of hormones, genes and sexual arousal has been opened.
sexual motivation and sexual arousal are complex phenomena that are likely to involve many different brain regions and different neurochemical mechanisms.
the study of the molecular and cellular bases of mammalian sexual behavior and sexual arousal is a work in progress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sexual arousal is a complex phenomenon, with many components, including the activation of the sympathetic-adrenomedullary system, the release of oxytocin, the activation of the medial amygdala and the activation of the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus.
the female reproductive behavior, lordosis, is a complex behavior, and that its expression is controlled by the coordinated actions of multiple genes.
the female reproductive system is controlled by a complex of interacting genes and hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the brain mechanisms underlying the expression and control of specific natural behaviors can be delineated, and that the mechanisms underlying general arousal and motivational states are likely to be more complicated and less amenable to simple analysis.
sexual arousal, as well as other forms of motivational arousal, is likely to be a composite of multiple, separable processes.
there are two distinct components of sexual arousal, one related to general arousal, and the other related to the sexual nature of the stimulus.
